official.deadline_note: Applications for the 2026/2027 round had to be submitted in the CGS system before February 8, 2026; the embassy then sent all recommended applications to the China Scholarship Council between February 9 and March 5, 2026. No deadline for a subsequent cycle has been published as of 10 October 2026.
official.status_note: The Embassy announced on 27 October 2025 that the 2026/2027 Chinese Government Scholarship 'is now open for application', with the online application and documents required in the system before February 8, 2026. That deadline has passed and admission results were available in the system in July to August 2026; no 2027/2028 round dates have been published on the Embassy's updates page as of 10 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The China Scholarship Council publishes 'Tuition fees' as the first item of Chinese Government Scholarship coverage, and the Embassy describes this programme as a 'Full scholarship' that 'does not include international travel expenses'.
benefits: Full scholarship under the China - Indonesia Scholarship in Higher Education Program, with 20 places for undergraduate/master's/doctoral programs (it is used for recruiting students who go to China to study marine, medical, health, tourism, education and other required majors)
Free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy
Stipend: Undergraduates: CNY 2,500 per month; Master's students/general scholars: CNY 3,000 per month; Doctoral students/senior scholars: CNY 3,500 per month
Comprehensive medical insurance: CNY 800 per person per year; CNY 400 per person (for programs lasting less than six months)
Does not include international travel expenses
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country other than the People's Republic of China, and be in good health both mentally and physically
Be a high school graduate under the age of 25 when applying for undergraduate programs
Be a bachelor's degree holder under the age of 35 when applying for master's programs, and a master's degree holder under the age of 40 when applying for doctoral programs

Be a high school graduate (at least) under the age of 45 when applying for general scholar programs, and a master's degree holder or an associate professor (or above) under the age of 50 when applying for senior scholar programs
Take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) and upload a valid score report when applying for bachelor programs

Have acquired the Chinese proficiency of HSK Level 3 for Chinese-taught general scholar and senior scholar programs and HSK Level 4 for Chinese-taught master's or doctoral programs; applicants who obtained their degree from a Chinese university using Chinese as the teaching language do not need to provide relevant language proficiency certificates; meet the admission requirements of the applied universities in terms of academic ability, language proficiency and other relevant criteria
requirements: Submit the online application and corresponding application documents in the system at www.campuschina.org before February 8, 2026, using Indonesian Agency Number 3602; no paper materials need to be sent to the embassy
Obtain Pre-Admission Documents from the chosen Chinese universities before submitting the online application - at least one pre-admission document from the universities applied for is required

Bachelor's applicants must register for and take the CSCA before the application deadline and obtain a valid Score Report; applicants intending to enrol in September 2026 were required to register and take the CSCA on December 21, 2025 or January 25, 2026

Applicants for master's, doctoral, general scholar and senior scholar programs taught in Chinese must submit a valid HSK score report meeting the corresponding Chinese language proficiency requirements; applicants for programs taught in other languages must provide relevant language proficiency certificates, such as IELTS or TOEFL score reports, in accordance with the requirements of each university
Uploaded supporting documents must be clear, authentic and valid; applicants shall bear the consequences caused by unclear or unidentifiable uploaded materials

Chinese Government Scholarship students are not allowed to obtain other scholarships (excluding one-time awards) established by the Chinese government at all levels and the admitted universities at the same time
documents: Application Form for Chinese Government Scholarship (in Chinese or English)

Passport Home Page: clear scanned copy of the information page of an ordinary passport; if the validity period is less than 12 months calculated from the expected start date of study, renew the passport and use it for the application

Notarized highest diploma (prospective diploma winners must submit official proof of student status from their current school) and academic transcripts; documents in languages other than Chinese or English must be attached with notarized Chinese or English translations

Language qualification certificates: valid HSK score report for Chinese-taught master's, doctoral, general scholar and senior scholar programs, or IELTS/TOEFL-type certificates for programs taught in other languages, plus a CSCA Score Report for applicants seeking a bachelor's degree

Pre-Admission Documents issued by the universities applied for, such as a pre-admission notice from the international students' admission department or an invitation letter from the schools or professors; at least one is required

Study Plan or Research Proposal in Chinese or English (minimum 200 words for undergraduates, 500 words for non-degree students and 800 words for postgraduates), two recommendation letters from professors or associate professors for graduate or senior scholar programs, Example of Art/Other Supporting Documents for art or design majors, valid documents of legal guardians in China for applicants under 18, a photocopy of the completed Foreigner Physical Examination Form for stays exceeding 6 months, and a valid Non-criminal record report issued within 6 months prior to submission
selection_criteria: The embassy sends all recommended applications to the China Scholarship Council for final review (February 9 to March 5, 2026)
The CSC will organize designated universities and experts concerned to examine applicants' eligibility and academic performance before finalizing the short-list candidates
CSCA score report will be one of the necessary materials for admission review by universities for bachelor programs
Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the applied universities in terms of academic ability, language proficiency and other relevant criteria
coverage: Free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy
Stipend: CNY 2,500 per month for undergraduates; CNY 3,000 per month for master's students/general scholars; CNY 3,500 per month for doctoral students/senior scholars
Comprehensive medical insurance: CNY 800 per person per year; CNY 400 per person for programs lasting less than six months
Does not include international travel expenses
application_method: Online application and document upload in the China Scholarship Council system at www.campuschina.org, using Indonesian Agency Number 3602
No paper materials need to be sent to the embassy
The embassy forwards recommended applications to the China Scholarship Council between February 9 and March 5, 2026, and applicants check admission results in the system in July to August 2026
official.application_route: Apply online at www.campuschina.org under Indonesian Agency Number 3602 after securing a pre-admission document from the target university; the Embassy reviews and forwards recommended applications to the China Scholarship Council.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of a country other than the People's Republic of China; this channel receives applications through the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Indonesia under Indonesian Agency Number 3602
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is open to non-Chinese citizens, and for this programme applications are filed with the Chinese Embassy in Indonesia rather than directly with universities
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: 20 places for undergraduate/master's/doctoral programs, used for recruiting students who go to China to study marine, medical, health, tourism, education and other required majors
official.research_requirement: A Study Plan or Research Proposal in Chinese or English with a minimum of 200 words for undergraduates, 500 words for non-degree students and 800 words for postgraduates (the CSC guide states no less than 1,000 words for postgraduates); graduate and senior scholar applicants must also submit two recommendation letters from professors or associate professors
official.duration: Covers both major study and Chinese language (preparatory) study: 'The language courses last one year, whereas the duration of the scholarship for major study conforms to that as required'
official.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship is set up by the Chinese government for talented students and scholars to pursue higher education or conduct research in Chinese universities, with the China Scholarship Council, entrusted by China's Ministry of Education, responsible for admission, enrollment and administration. Through the China-Indonesia Scholarship in Higher Education Program, the Embassy of the PRC in Indonesia offers 20 full scholarships for undergraduate, master's and doctoral study in China for students going to China to study marine, medical, health, tourism, education and other required majors; the award does not include international travel expenses.
official.program_type: China - Indonesia Scholarship in Higher Education Program (Chinese Government Scholarship)
official.english_requirement: No single English test score is published. Applicants for programs taught in other languages are required to provide relevant language proficiency certificates, such as IELTS or TOEFL score reports, in accordance with the requirements of each university; Chinese-taught master's and doctoral programs require HSK Level 4 and Chinese-taught general/senior scholar programs require HSK Level 3, while bachelor's applicants must submit a valid CSCA score report.

per-level programme duration (CSC states only that major-study duration conforms to programme requirements, with one year of Chinese preparatory study)
dates for any cycle after 2026/2027 (none published as of 10 October 2026)
verification.notes: Award amounts and coverage taken from the China Scholarship Council's own Application Guide page on campuschina.org; headline funding_amount is the doctoral stipend rate (CNY 3,500/month) because CSC publishes tiered stipends - CNY 2,500 undergraduate, CNY 3,000 master's/general scholar, CNY 3,500 doctoral/senior scholar per month. The Embassy page confirms the 20-place Indonesia channel, agency number 3602, the 8 February 2026 deadline and the explicit exclusion of international travel expenses.

applicant_utility.summary: This is Indonesia's designated channel of the Chinese Government Scholarship: 20 full awards coordinated by the Embassy in Jakarta and applied for entirely online through the CSC system at campuschina.org under agency number 3602. The package covers tuition, accommodation plus a monthly stipend (CNY 2,500 undergraduate, 3,000 master's, 3,500 doctoral) and comprehensive medical insurance, but you fund your own flights and visa costs. The real bottleneck is the pre-admission document - you must already hold a pre-admission notice or professor invitation from your target university before the portal will accept your application, so university outreach has to start months ahead of the early-February deadline. Bachelor's applicants face an extra scheduling constraint because the CSCA test sittings for a September intake fall before the application window closes.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Indonesian or other non-PRC nationals applying via Indonesia who can secure a professor's invitation early and want fully funded marine, medical, health, tourism or education study in China.
application_readiness_checklist: Start emailing target university international offices and professors in September-October to secure the pre-admission notice or invitation letter - nothing can be submitted without at least one
Register for the CSCA in the December or January sitting if you are a bachelor's applicant, and confirm the required test subjects directly with your target institution
Renew your passport if it expires within 12 months of your expected study start date
Have your diploma and transcripts notarised with certified English/Chinese translations before the portal opens
Schedule the Foreigner Physical Examination and police clearance so both remain inside their 6-month validity at submission
Scan documents on a professional flatbed scanner and check every uploaded page for legibility - unreadable uploads are your responsibility
common_rejection_risks: Applications submitted without any pre-admission document from the applied university
Passport validity under 12 months from the expected start date of study
Blurry, cropped or unidentifiable uploads - the Embassy states applicants bear the consequences
Missing or invalid CSCA score report for bachelor's applicants, which universities treat as a necessary material for admission review
HSK level not matching the programme level (Level 3 for scholar programmes, Level 4 for Chinese-taught master's and doctoral programmes)
Holding or concealing another Chinese government or university scholarship, which voids the award and triggers a three-year application ban
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International airfare to and from China, visa and residence-permit fees, travel to test centres and hospitals for the CSCA and physical examination, notarisation and translation fees, any rent shortfall if the free dormitory or accommodation subsidy does not cover actual housing costs, and day-to-day living costs beyond the monthly stipend.
document_audit: Study-plan word counts conflict between official pages - the Embassy sets 800 words as the postgraduate minimum while the CSC guide says no less than 1,000; write to the stricter figure
Recommendation letters must come from professors or associate professors - letters from employers or lecturers do not meet the published rule
The Foreigner Physical Examination Form is invalid without the attending physician's signature, the hospital's official stamp and a sealed photograph, and results are valid for only 6 months
The non-criminal record report must usually have been issued within 6 months prior to the submission date of the application
Applicants under 18 must additionally submit valid documents of their legal guardians in China
Transcripts and diplomas in languages other than Chinese or English need notarised translations attached
alerts: The 8 February 2026 deadline for the 2026/2027 round has passed and results were released in the system in July-August 2026; no 2027/2028 dates had been published on the Embassy site as of 10 October 2026, and the previous cycle was announced in late October, so monitor the Embassy updates page now
You cannot hold any other Chinese government or admitted-university scholarship (one-time awards excepted) at the same time; concealment means cancellation, repayment and a three-year ban
CSCA test sittings for a September 2026 intake (21 December 2025 and 25 January 2026) sit before the application deadline, so the test calendar - not the portal - sets your timeline
The award explicitly excludes international travel expenses, so budget for flights and the visa on top of the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create and submit the CGS application with all documents in the campuschina.org system under agency number 3602; the Embassy reviews and forwards the recommended list to the China Scholarship Council between 9 February and 5 March, CSC and designated universities decide the shortlist, and applicants check results in the system in July-August.
